The Premise

What "AI in Agriculture" Actually Means

AI in agriculture is the application of machine learning, computer vision, and data systems to farming and the wider agrifood chain — from a seedling in a nursery to produce on a shelf. It spans precision agriculture, autonomous machinery, post-harvest quality control, yield forecasting, and the policy that decides who benefits from all of it.

Dr. Maryna Kuzmenko is a speaker and trainer on AI in agriculture who works at exactly that intersection — technical innovation, public policy, and commercial viability. The throughline of this work is human-first: technology should widen access for smallholders and specialists alike, not just optimise the largest operations.

Questions, Answered

AI in Agriculture FAQ

What is AI in agriculture?

AI in agriculture is the use of machine learning, computer vision, and data systems across farming and the agrifood chain — including precision agriculture, autonomous machinery, post-harvest quality control, yield forecasting, and supply-chain optimisation.

Is the AI in Agriculture course free?

Yes. AI in Agriculture: Practical Introductory Course is free to enrol on aiinagriculture.org: 15 video lessons (1h 14m) and 8 quizzes, marked server-side, with a certificate anyone can verify. No technical background is required. 80:20, the monthly report, is £1 a month by subscription.

Who is Dr. Maryna Kuzmenko?

Dr. Maryna Kuzmenko is a speaker and trainer on AI in agriculture, LinkedIn Top Voice, founder of MooMore and co-founder of Petiole. She won the Innovate UK Women in Innovation Award 2025/26 for MooMore, and has taught AI in agriculture to 3.4K+ students across 129 countries. About Maryna →

What are the main applications of AI in agriculture?

The most established applications are precision agriculture, computer-vision quality control for produce and nursery stock, predictive analytics for yield and risk, autonomous machinery, and decision support that helps growers reduce waste while improving output.

Where can I learn about AI in agriculture?

Start with the free course on aiinagriculture.org, then subscribe to 80:20 for a monthly read on what changed. You can also follow the AI in Agriculture newsletter on LinkedIn, watch explainers on YouTube, or read The Precision Vineyard. For organisations, a guest lecture or workshop is the usual route.

Has Maryna Kuzmenko written a book on AI in agriculture?

Yes. She writes the AI in Agriculture series: The Precision Vineyard: A Grower's Field Guide to AI, Sensors and Robotics (book 1) covers what to adopt, what to skip, and what it pays back in viticulture, and Seed Quality Control (book 2) is a practical guide to imaging and automation in vegetable seed. She also wrote Vertical Farming: A Guide for Growing Minds. See the books page.

How can I book Maryna to speak on AI in agriculture?

Visit the speaking page to see signature topics and formats, then use the contact page to check availability for your event.
